title: Direct Knowledge Of Allah 19th Degree 1st Truth Applying The Principle To The Cosmos

questions.question: What two things are used as examples at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: A fine book and a well-made house.

questions.question: What action must happen for a book to exist?
questions.answer: Someone must write it.

questions.question: What action must happen for a house to exist?
questions.answer: Someone must build it.

questions.question: If someone is called a writer or a builder, what does that show?
questions.answer: That person has that work and skill.

questions.question: Can an action happen all by itself with no one doing it?
questions.answer: No. An action needs someone who does it.

questions.question: Can a skill exist without a person who has that skill?
questions.answer: No. A skill belongs to someone.

questions.question: Can a craft exist without a craftsperson?
questions.answer: No. A craft needs a maker.

questions.question: Based on this rule, what is the universe compared to?
questions.answer: It is compared to many books and many buildings.

questions.question: Are the things in the universe said to give one small sign or many signs?
questions.answer: Many signs.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a beautiful book?
questions.answer: To show that careful work points to a maker.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a strong house?
questions.answer: To show that building points to a builder.

questions.question: If you see writing, what can you know?
questions.answer: A writer must be there.

questions.question: If you see a built place, what can you know?
questions.answer: A builder must be there.

questions.question: What simple rule is taught about deeds?
questions.answer: Every deed has a doer.

questions.question: What simple rule is taught about names like writer and builder?
questions.answer: They point to a real one with that name.

questions.question: What simple rule is taught about crafts?
questions.answer: Every craft has a craftsperson.

questions.question: How does the passage describe all the beings in the universe together?
questions.answer: Like many deep writings and many made structures.

questions.question: What does the picture of a pen teach about the universe?
questions.answer: It teaches that the universe is written in an ordered way.

questions.question: Do the beings in the universe point only one by one, or also all together?
questions.answer: Both one by one and all together.

questions.question: What kind of book is spoken about in the passage?
questions.answer: A book that is lovely and full of meaning.

questions.question: What kind of house is spoken about in the passage?
questions.answer: A house made in a good and careful way.

questions.question: Why is a book a good example for this lesson?
questions.answer: Because a book does not appear without someone making it.

questions.question: Why is a house a good example for this lesson?
questions.answer: Because a house does not stand there without someone building it.

questions.question: What do the names for jobs show, like writer and builder?
questions.answer: They show real workers and their work.

questions.question: What do writing and building tell us besides the person’s name?
questions.answer: They tell us the person has ability and qualities.

questions.question: What would be impossible, according to the passage: a deed without a doer or a deed with a doer?
questions.answer: A deed without a doer.

questions.question: What would be impossible, according to the passage: an attribute without anyone who has it or an attribute in someone?
questions.answer: An attribute without anyone who has it.

questions.question: How is the whole universe pictured after these examples?
questions.answer: As many meaningful writings and many built places.

questions.question: Does the passage describe the universe as random or arranged?
questions.answer: Arranged.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare beings to letters and books?
questions.answer: Because they carry signs that can be understood.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare beings to houses and palaces?
questions.answer: Because they look made, ordered, and set up with care.

questions.question: What can each created thing say by its existence?
questions.answer: That it has a Maker.

questions.question: When you see a nicely made book, what should you think about first?
questions.answer: The one who wrote it.

questions.question: When you see a nicely made house, what should you think about first?
questions.answer: The one who built it.

questions.question: What do good writing and good building tell us about the maker?
questions.answer: The maker has skill and ability.

questions.question: Why can’t a name like builder be empty?
questions.answer: Because it must belong to someone real.

questions.question: Why can’t a quality stand alone?
questions.answer: Because a quality must be in someone.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about work and worker?
questions.answer: Work shows there is a worker.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about art and artist?
questions.answer: Art shows there is an artist.

questions.question: How does the passage ask us to look at the universe?
questions.answer: As something made with meaning and order.

questions.question: What two big picture words are used for the universe?
questions.answer: Writings and buildings.

questions.question: Why might the universe be compared to many letters?
questions.answer: Because even small things carry signs.

questions.question: Why might the universe be compared to palaces?
questions.answer: Because it is full of design and careful making.

questions.question: Do single beings alone give proof, or do all beings together also give proof?
questions.answer: Both do.

questions.question: What kind of message do all beings give?
questions.answer: That there is one who made them.

questions.question: What must come before there can be writing?
questions.answer: A writer’s action.

questions.question: What must come before there can be a built home?
questions.answer: A builder’s action.

questions.question: What comes after the action in the passage’s chain of ideas?
questions.answer: The name of the one who does it.

questions.question: After the name, what does the passage say we understand?
questions.answer: The person has skills and qualities.

questions.question: After skills and qualities, what final truth do we understand?
questions.answer: There must be someone who truly has them.

questions.question: What is one impossible thing named in the passage about actions?
questions.answer: An action with no doer.

questions.question: What is one impossible thing named in the passage about names?
questions.answer: A name with no real one for it.

questions.question: What is one impossible thing named in the passage about qualities?
questions.answer: A quality with no one who has it.

questions.question: What is one impossible thing named in the passage about crafts?
questions.answer: A craft with no craftsperson.

questions.question: What does the passage say the universe is like in one picture?
questions.answer: A big group of meaningful writings.

questions.question: What does the passage say the universe is like in another picture?
questions.answer: A huge group of buildings and palaces.

questions.question: How many ways do the beings speak as signs by themselves and together?
questions.answer: In very many ways.

questions.question: What truth are they all bearing witness to?
questions.answer: That Allah is the Maker.

questions.question: Which is made with words in the passage’s example: a book or a house?
questions.answer: A book.

questions.question: Which is made by building in the passage’s example: a book or a house?
questions.answer: A house.

questions.question: What do both examples have in common?
questions.answer: Both need a maker.

questions.question: What do the job names in the passage help us know?
questions.answer: They help us know there is a real person doing the work.

questions.question: What do the person’s abilities help us know?
questions.answer: They help us know the maker is qualified for the work.

questions.question: Why is “deed without a doer” rejected in the passage?
questions.answer: Because work cannot happen by itself.

questions.question: Why is “craft without a craftsperson” rejected in the passage?
questions.answer: Because making needs a maker.

questions.question: What does the passage use as a rule for understanding the world?
questions.answer: Made things point to the one who made them.

questions.question: How is the universe described when thinking about knowledge and meaning?
questions.answer: Like deep books and letters.

questions.question: How is the universe described when thinking about making and strength?
questions.answer: Like buildings and palaces.

questions.question: What do these comparisons teach about the things inside the universe?
questions.answer: They are arranged and made on purpose.

questions.question: Does each thing give a sign only once, or in many ways?
questions.answer: In many ways.

questions.question: When all things are looked at together, what do they still show?
questions.answer: They still show one Divine Maker.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the passage?
questions.answer: Creation points to the Creator.
